newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures drop, all contracts limit-down.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures drop, all contracts limit-down.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures plunged on Wednesday, with all contracts down by the daily 500-yen limit at the close on active sales by local investors, traders said.
Benchmark September was down 500 yen at 17,800, with daily volume today at 77,627 lots. Open interest fell to 518,975 lots as of September 3 from the record 523,256 as of August 14.

Selling by individual investors emerged from the open due to weaker CBOT corn overnight, traders said. Further losses in CBOT overnight trading accelerated the bearish mood later, they said. "There was a phenomenon of jumping on the bandwagon today. Bearishness dominated the market," a trader said.
The spot September contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.64 per bushel at 0820 GMT, against $3.66-3/4 at Tuesday's close.
The spot September CBOT soybean futures contract on the overnight trading system was at $8.06 per bushel at 0820 GMT, from $8.11 at Tuesday's close.
